researched_by: the council's own parking pages and newsroom, committee reporting in the local press, and the 2021 staycation infrastructure announcements
policy_summary:
Moray has spent five years building the facilities before it would allow the stay, and in 2026 it finally allowed the stay - for two vehicles, in one village, at a fee it does not intend to enforce.

The sequence matters. In 2021 the council put GBP850,000 of staycation support behind 'stopover sites with waste disposal, car parking enhancements and increased signage' at Burghead, Portknockie, Craigellachie, Ballindalloch, Cullen, Lossiemouth, Portgordon and Findhorn, of which GBP20,000 went on chargeable campervan waste disposal points and chargeable water at five: Burghead harbour, Portknockie harbour, Portgordon car park, Fiddich Park at Craigellachie and Cragganmore at Ballindalloch, at a charge set at GBP6.82. The council was explicit at the time that 'informal camping will not be encouraged'. Somewhere to empty, nowhere to sleep.

Overnight parking took four more years. A consultation ran from 17 April to 16 May 2025 on nine provisional locations - Lossiemouth, Cullen, Buckie, Forres, Portgordon, Burghead, Ballindalloch, Craigellachie and Aberlour - and drew more than 2,200 responses: 74% of Moray residents and 95% of non-residents in favour, most content with GBP7 a night, and over two thirds content with a 6pm to 10am window. On 11 November 2025 the Economic Development and Infrastructure Services Committee approved a single 12-month pilot at Station Road car park, Burghead, chosen for its nearby waste facilities and strong local backing. It runs 1 April to 30 November 2026: a maximum of two self-contained campervans or motorhomes, 6pm to 10am, one night only, GBP7 through PayByPhone under location code 811845, no awnings, chairs or generators, and no facilities on site beyond the harbour waste point nearby.

The fee is voluntary. That is the detail everything else turns on - the council's own committee debate had a member questioning whether goodwill would collect it, and the honest reading of a two-bay voluntary scheme is that this is a monitoring exercise dressed as provision. Nine sites consulted, one delivered, two vehicles.

No prohibition instrument was found anywhere in Moray. No traffic regulation order, no byelaw, no signed overnight ban at Findhorn, Lossiemouth, Hopeman or Cullen came to light, and the council's off-street parking order text was not published in any readable form. That absence is itself uncertain rather than a finding - see open questions.
notes:
MORAY IS THE MIRROR IMAGE OF ABERDEENSHIRE NEXT DOOR. Aberdeenshire owns caravan parks it does not run and prohibits overnight sleeping in every car park it does. Moray runs no caravan parks at all, has never published a prohibition, and has built service infrastructure at eight coastal and Speyside locations. Same coast, same NC500 eastern leg traffic, opposite instincts.

STEP 2 CAME BACK EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE ANSWER. Every caravan site on the Moray coast checks out as private or community: Findochty Caravan Park at Jubilee Terrace is 'a small, family run site' of 25-30 touring pitches, West Beach at Hopeman recently changed hands privately, Silver Sands at Lossiemouth is a holiday park, Cullen Bay, Burghead Beach, Findhorn Bay, Findhorn Sands, North Alves, Strathlene at Buckie, Speyside Gardens and Riverside at Elgin are all commercial. The council holds no caravan park on its books, runs no country park campsite, and the closest it comes to owning overnight supply is the harbour waste points. Findhorn's 21-space motorhome stopover on West Beach car park is run by The Findhorn Village Conservation Company, a charity, with ANPR barrier and online booking at findhornparking.com and a two-night limit - Moray Council granted it planning permission in October 2020 and nothing more. Do not attribute it to the council.

THE TRADE OBJECTED EARLY AND LOUDLY. In April 2021 the manager of Strathlene caravan park in Buckie attacked the service-point programme in the local press - 'the council do not seem to have a clue what the problem is with motorhomes and campervans' - arguing the council should enforce against wild camping and send people to commercial parks instead of building competing facilities, and objecting specifically to two proposed stops within seven miles of existing parks. The council's line was that the sites are 'complimentary to rather than in competition with local sites'. This is the same British Holiday and Home Parks Association argument that shadowed the Highland scheme, made locally.

ABERLOUR IS THE ONE TO WATCH. At the November 2025 committee, Councillor Juli Harris moved to add Alice Littler Park at Aberlour to the pilot, seconded by Councillor Neil Cameron. It was deferred to March 2026 for budget work and community consultation. Whether it was approved in March 2026 was not established, and it is the single most likely near-term addition.

TOMINTOUL IS IN MORAY BUT IS RECORDED IN data/sites/cairngorms-national-park.json AS THE TOMINTOUL BOWLING CLUB CARAVAN SITE. It is a landowner-policy community site inside the national park, not council provision, and is deliberately not duplicated here.

SCALE CHECK. The 2021 investment figures are small: GBP20,000 across five waste points out of a GBP850,000 package, and press coverage of the 2026 pilot put the overnight scheme's payback at roughly GBP11,000 of investment against income that would take decades to recover it. Moray is not making money on this and does not appear to be trying to.
open_questions: Does The Moray Council's off-street parking order contain the standard 'no sleeping, camping or cooking' clause that Aberdeenshire and most Scottish councils rely on? No order text was published in readable form, so whether an overnight stay outside the Burghead bays is merely unprovided-for or actually prohibited is unresolved. This is the biggest gap in the file.
Was Alice Littler Park at Aberlour added to the pilot when the deferred amendment returned in March 2026?

Are the five campervan waste and water points at Burghead harbour, Portknockie harbour, Portgordon car park, Fiddich Park Craigellachie and Cragganmore Ballindalloch all still operating in 2026, and is the charge still GBP6.82? The council publishes no current page for them.

Exact coordinates of Station Road car park, Burghead, and how many bays the car park holds in total. The council gives no postcode, map or grid reference for it and no independent stopover directory lists it.

Is the GBP7 genuinely voluntary, or is it enforced under the parking order? STV and the local press both report it as a voluntary payment; the council's own page presents it as a charge to be paid through PayByPhone.

Whether any overnight parking prohibition signage exists at Findhorn, Lossiemouth East and West beaches, Hopeman, Cullen or Portknockie. None was found, but absence of evidence in a county this small is weak evidence of absence.

sites.price_note: GBP7 a night, reported by STV and the Forres Gazette as a VOLUNTARY payment; the council's page presents it as a charge payable through PayByPhone location code 811845 or 01224 440871
facilities: campervan waste disposal at Burghead Harbour nearby
sites.search_hint: Station Road car park, Burghead, Moray - Moray Council campervan overnight parking pilot, PayByPhone location 811845
sites.notes:
THE ONLY LEGITIMATE COUNCIL OVERNIGHT STOP IN MORAY, and it holds two vehicles. Approved by the Economic Development and Infrastructure Services Committee on 11 November 2025 as a 12-month pilot after a consultation that drew over 2,200 responses with 74% resident and 95% non-resident support. Self-contained vehicles only, one night, 6pm to 10am, nothing outside the van. Burghead was picked over the eight other consulted locations because the harbour waste point is already there and the community backed it. Results go back to committee before any wider roll-out.

COORDINATES DELIBERATELY LEFT NULL. Neither the council's page nor its newsroom, the committee reporting, or any stopover directory gives a postcode, map link or grid reference for this car park, and it appears in no motorhome database. Rather than pin it on the village centre, it is left unplaced. It needs one satellite check by somebody who can open a map - Station Road, Burghead, IV30, on the peninsula east of the harbour.

sites.name: Alice Littler Park, Aberlour
sites.notes: Proposed as a second pilot site by Councillor Juli Harris at the 11 November 2025 committee, seconded by Councillor Neil Cameron. The amendment was DEFERRED TO MARCH 2026 for budget review and community consultation, with officers advising that costs would be 'similar' to Burghead but needed verifying, and Councillor Cameron noting the two parks 'are two very different' locations. Whether it was approved in March 2026 is unestablished. Recorded because it is the most likely next addition to a scheme that currently consists of two bays; treat as a proposal, not a place to stay.
